name: Modern SEO - M4L5 What Happens When You Outgrow Modern SEO
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 4 Client Acquisition and Pricing](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-4-client-acquisition-and-pricing) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
The course closer (3:32). The three-step method handles 70 to 80% of clients (instructor claim) and Core 30 covers competitive markets, but some situations need more. Most of the lesson pitches the paid Pro group.

# Three signs a client needs advanced strategies
1. **Plateau despite proper implementation:** rank maps stuck at very low green (audio: 5%, 10% or less; slide: 10 to 15%).
2. **Very competitive market:** examples are downtown Chicago personal injury lawyers, Beverly Hills plastic surgeons, Manhattan dentists.
3. **Complex technical issues:** 500+ pages ranking poorly even at the business's own location.

# Key concepts
- **Toolkit recap:** three-step method, Core 30, gap analysis, Facebook Ads, networking, content, profitable pricing.
- **Pro adds** (paid): Core 30 implementation workflows, advanced content strategies, technical troubleshooting and industry tactics, a 90-day challenge record (building a $10,000 a month agency with no sales calls, in progress at recording), weekly Zoom huddles.
- **When to upgrade:** naturally, when a competitive market or complex technical case appears. Until then, "implement what you've learned. Work with real clients. Master the fundamentals."
- **Closing advice:** "Start with one client. Apply the three-step method. Get them results. Then do it again."

# Checklist
- Three-step method (and Core 30 where used) implemented correctly before calling a plateau.
- Rank map green coverage checked; market competitiveness assessed.
- Large sites checked for poor rankings at their own location.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Run the three-sign check on [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub) against current rank maps in [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas).
- Alphalete matches sign 3 (large, mostly programmatic site with very few pages indexed per Kim's memory); per M4L4, scope that technical work separately. See [GSC Indexing Tracker](lib:brain-gsc-indexing-tracker).
- Pro is paid; noted only and would need Kim's approval. Its visible topics (Optimizing for ChatGPT, Technical Audit, Reduce Client Churn, Managing Large Websites) overlap TAG's work, which may help decide whether to ask Scott.

# Caveats and open questions
- Plateau number conflicts with the 10 to 15% Core 30 trigger in Modules 2 and 3; this sign may mean "still stuck after Core 30" (unclear).
- Technical threshold 500+ here vs 450 in M3L1; none firm.
- The 90-day challenge status is unknown.
